- Discussion of drug prohibition in Canada started in the early 1900s as a response to opium - HIST-3790: Opium and the making of the modern world

- Opium and Narcotics Drug Act passed in 1920; [Controlled Drugs and Substances Act (last ammended July 2026)](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/c-38.8/){target="_blank"}

- Resources to learn more about the [history of drug policy and other social considerations with drugs in Canada](https://drugpolicy.ca){target="_blank"} ## Drug Identification - Several major challenges (that can be addressed with new developments in science and technology) - Backlogs - Personnel turn around / training / lack of funding, *emerging drugs* - Novel Psychoactive Substances (Designer Drugs) - [Making $3 million dollars of fentanyl using $3,600 and a web browser](https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/drugs-fentanyl-supplychain/){target="_blank"} - Lack of reference data, isomers, may need new SOPs, reporting criteria, for each new drug - Sample complexity - Highly toxic drugs means that street samples actually have minor amounts of controlled material ## Drug Identification - Some analytical solutions currently being researched include - Fast GC-MS; GC coupled with Cold EI-MS - Ambient Ionization Mass Spectrometry - GC-VUV / GC-IR - Benchtop NMR

- [Better data sharing and collaboration](https://www.nist.gov/publications/towards-increased-data-sharing-and-standardization-illicit-drug-analysis-and-monitoring){target="_blank"} between forensic labs and cognate research areas (e.g., public health, intelligence) - [Article: Forensic seized drug analysis: Current challenges and emerging analytical techniques](https://doi.org/10.1002%2Fwfs2.1486){target="_blank"} ::: {.notes} VUV - vacuum ultra violet spectroscopy ::: ## Chemical Weapons - The **convention on the prohibition of the development, production, stockpiling, and use of chemical weapons and of their destruction (the CWC)** was signed in 1993 and put into force in 1997

- *Chemical weapons* includes: - Munitions, devices, equipment specifically designed for employing munitions - [Toxic chemicals and their precursors](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/0470012285#page=141){target="blank"} - 57 line items: 42 individual compounds and 15 families of compounds (e.g., VX) ## Chemical Weapons ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=50%} Organization for the prohibition of chemical weapons (OPCW) was established by countries to enforce the CWC - verification studies - retrospective and incidence response type investigations ::: ::: {.column widht=50%} ![](../figures/OPCW.jpg){fig-aligned=center} ::: ::: ## Fire Investigations - Fires can be accidental or deliberate (arson). Potential motivations for deliberate fires include: - intent to cover up other crimes (theft, murder) - insurance fraud - civil disorder (e.g., vandalism) - malicious intent / terrorism

- Fire investigations begin **without certainty as to whether a crime has been committed** - Step 1 is to determine the merit of the assertion that the event is suspicious ## Fire Investigations - Traditionally broken into two different stages: - scene investigation to determine cause, origin and development/spread of fire - lab analysis of samples (when arson is suspected)

- Scene investigators need to know necessary conditions for fire to be initiated and maintained, how fires develop and spread (dynamics), different types of fuel, among other investigation skills

- Lab Analysts need to have skills with analytical instrumentation and an understanding of the nature of flammable materials and their pyrolysis and combustion products to analyze fire residue/debris ## Fire Investigations - Some relevant material properties include: ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=10%} ::: ::: {.column width=90%} ::: {style="font-size:0.6em;"} - **Flammability (explosive) limits/ranges:** outside of these limits, the fuel-vapor to air concentration will be too lean or too rich to ignite (e.g., the lower FL for 100 octane petrol is 1.4%, the upper FL is 7.6%) - **Vapor density:** density of the fuel vapor relative to the density of air (density less than 1 will spread out at the ceiling, density greater than 1 will spread out at the floor) - **Flash point:** lowest temperature at which a liquid fuel produces a flammable vapor - **Flame point:** the lowest temperature at which a liquid fuel produces enough flammable vapor that it can be ignited - **Auto-ignition temperature (AIT):** temperature at which a fuel will ignite without any additional source of ignition ::: ::: ::: - Knowing a material's properties only helpful if you know what the material is ## Fire Investigations - Significant research in fire investigation: [(Interpol Review)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2589871X26000422){target="_blank"}

- Fire scenes are hard: sample quality is poor (post fire extinguishing, a lot of components in a fuel, and weathering) - On-site chemical analysis - Models - Laboratory reconstructions (e.g., weathering studies) - Computer models ## Fire Investigations - [The Fire Behaviour of Fabrics Containing Dried Emollient Residues](https://www.mdpi.com/2571-6255/8/4/133){target="_blank"} - Proof-of-concept study - **Objective:** Investigate the flammability of fabrics containing dried emollient on fabrics - **Results:** Fabrics that have dried emollients are very flammable ## Fire Investigations - [Artificial intelligence and thermodynamics help solving arson cases](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-77516-x){target="_blank"} - Proof-of-concept study - **Objective:** demonstrate how combining machine learning, thermodynamic modeling and quantum mechanics can predict the composition of unweathererd gasoline samples starting from weathered ones - **Results:** Built and an NN model assuming an *ideal case*, where all composition change in gasoline is due exclusively to evaporation (and not adsorption, pyrolysis, degradation, extinguishing material) ## Death Investigation - Post-mortem examinations are carried out by pathologists to try and determine cause of death

- Post-mortem examinations begin **without certainty as to whether a crime has been committed**

- Time since death is an important factor when trying to determine the cause of death - post-mortem interval (PMI) estimatition techniques are methods for approximating time since death ## Death Investigation - Several established techniques for PMI estimation: - Pathology (looking at post-mortom changes to the body) - Entomology (insect activity)

- Newer techniques being researched: - DNA quantification (e.g., methylation) - Biomarker discovery - "OMICS" (metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics) - Looking at body (skin, hair, bones), environment (soil, water, air), microbes ## Death Investigation - [The ‘ForensOMICS’ approach for postmortem interval estimation from human bone by integrating metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics](https://elifesciences.org/articles/83658){target="_blank"} - Proof-of-Concept study - **Objective:** To evaluate the utility of combining metabolomic, lipidomic, and proteomic analysis of human bone samples to estiamte PMI--"ForensOMICS" - **Results:** Showed that *fingerprints* of samples collected at different time points were best separated using metabolite information; infer that "ForensOMICS" can be used to estimate PMI ## Environmental Forensic Chemistry - A field that has developed over the past 70 years - A successor to drinking water quality studies

- Involves scientific investigation to: - Decipher the source(s) and fate(s) of environmental contaminants - Identify culprit

- Enforcement and protections of acts and regulations: [Environment and Climate Change Canada Acts & Regulations](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/corporate/transparency.html){target="_blank"} ## Environmental Forensic Chemistry - Environmental Protection Acts - The Department of the Environment Act - The Canada Water Act - International Rivers Improvement Act (IRIA) - Lake of the Woods Control Board Act - Weather Modification Act

- Pollution Prevention Acts - Canadian Environmental Protections Act - Fisheries Act - Antarctic Environmental Protections Act - Artic Waters Pollution Prevention Act ## Environmental Forensic Chemistry - Biodiversity and Conservation - Species at Risk Act - Migratory Birds Convention Act - Wild Animals and Plant Protection and Regulation of International and Interprovincial Trade Act - Canada Wildlife Act

- Sustainable Development - Federal Sustainable Development Act - Canada Foundation of Sustainable Development Technology Act ## Environmental Forensic Chemistry - The credibility of environmental forensic chemistry results is directly related to the quality of measurements and interpretations

- Some well-known challenges in measurement quality include: - Sensitivity / Specificity - Changing targets (laws and regulations) - *Sampling (environmental systems are complex)* ## Environmental Forensic Chemistry - **Case Study:** Characterizing Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)

- **PFAS:** group of thousands of synthetic chemicals that are used in consumer products and industrial processes - Non-stick cookware, cosmetics, cleaning products, food packaging - fire-fightig foam, *lab equipment*

- Discovered in the 1930s; commonly used since the 1950s; started noticing environmental persistence and health effects in humans in the 1970s; subject of *some* environmental protection since 2000s

## Environmental Forensic Chemistry - Known health effects in animals: - liver damage, immune system malfunction, reproductive and developmental issues, tumors

- Suspected health effects (correlations) in humans: - liver damage, increased serum cholesterol, decreased vaccination response, decreased birth weight, increased chance of thyroid disease, cardiovascular issues, cancer

- Several governing bodies have created standards for allowable levels of specific PFAS in consumer products and the environment ## Environmental Forensic Chemistry - [Source attribution of Poly- and Perfluoralkyl Substances (PFASs) in surface waters from Rhode Island and New York Metropolitan Area](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.estlett.6b00255){target="_blank"}

- **Objective:** Identify sources of surface water PFAS contamination in a specified geography - **Methods(summary):** - sampled water at 28 sites in Rhode Island and 9 sites in NY/NJ - samples were spiked with known amount of PFAS - PFAS were then extracted and then analyzed using LC/MS-MS - Statistical and spatial analysis ## White collar crimes - Illegal Timber trade ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=40%} Illegal logging is one of the [most profitable natural resource crimes](https://gfintegrity.org/report/transnational-crime-and-the-developing-world/){target="_blank"} - Species Identification / Origin Identification ::: ::: {.column widht=60%} :::{style="font-size:0.6em"} | Transnational Crime | Estimated Annual Value (USD) | |:--------------------|:---------------------------| | Counterfeiting | 923 billion to 1.13 trillion | | Drug Trafficking | 426 billion to 652 billion | | **Illegal Logging** | **52 billion to 157 billion** | | Human Trafficking | 150.2 billion | | Illegal Mining | 12 billion to 48 billion | | Illegal Fishing | 15.5 billion to 36.4 billion | | Illegal Wildlife Trade | 5 billion to 23 billion | | Crude Oil Theft | 5.2 billion to 11.9 billion | | Small Arms and Light Weapons Trafficking | 1.7 billion to 3.5 billion | | Organ Trafficking | 840 million to 1.7 billion | | Tracking in Cultural Property | 1.2 billion to 1.6 billion | Total | 1.6 trillion to 2.2 trillion ::: ::: ::: ## ![Illustration of Chemotype from [Deklerk (2023).](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fsiae.2022.100057){target="_blank"}](../figures/WoodIDFigure.png){fig-align=center} ## Coming up - Seminars are running in-person on Thursday October 8th (F01 and F02)

- Lecture next week: An introduction to (or refresher on) programming in R
